title: A reply a layer answered without the handler still echoes the peer's token

provenance.quote: If any NLIP message containing a submessage that where the format field is 'token', the end-point must include the same submessage with the exact same format, subformat and content in its response message to the peer end-point, except when the token was initially created by the end-point.

notes: The reading, and it is the first of five: §6.2's obligation attaches to the reply **on the wire**, not to the code path that produced it. The standard knows no layers — it names an "end-point" and says what its response message must contain — so an implementation with a message-level layer that answers on its own (a cache, a canned answer, a maintenance-mode layer) has to decide what such a reply owes, and nothing in ECMA-430 decides it. This corpus reads the clause as being about the message the peer receives, which makes the answer the same whoever produced it: `endpoint.short_circuit` is the case shape for that reading. Here the layer answered with a bare text message carrying no tokens, and the peer's `cli-1` is in the reply anyway. An implementation whose layers sit *above* clause 6 rather than inside it produces the same reply and passes; one that lets a layer out past the echo does not, and that is the point of the case rather than an accident of this workspace's composition.
